# onetsolutions_hosting_ftp_account (Resource)

Manages an FTP account of a web hosting, confined to one directory of it.

The account connects with `login` (`<username>@<domain of the web hosting>`) and only sees
`directory` and what is below it.

## Changes

`password` changes in place. It is never read back: it is kept in the state (marked sensitive)
and an import cannot recover it, so the first apply after an import sets the account's password to
the configured one, with a plan-time warning. `directory` and `quota_mb` cannot change in place: a
change recreates the account, which keeps the files of its directory, as a destroy does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

variable "ftp_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_ftp_account" "deploy" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  username   = "deploy"
  password   = var.ftp_password
  directory  = "/public_html/app"
}

output "ftp_login" {
  value = onetsolutions_hosting_ftp_account.deploy.login
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting. Changing it recreates the object in the other web hosting.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the account. Can be changed in place; after an import, the next apply sets the account's password to the configured one. At least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character. It is never read back: it is stored in the state, and an import cannot recover it.
- `username` (String) The username of the account: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 32 characters. Changing it recreates the account.

### Optional

- `directory` (String) The directory the account is confined to, relative to the web hosting's home directory, starting with `/` and without a trailing `/`, such as `/public_html/uploads`. Defaults to `/public_html`. Changing it recreates the account; the files stay.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `quota_mb` (Number) The disk quota of the account in MB; `0` (the default) means unlimited. Changing it recreates the account; the files stay.

### Read-Only

- `home_directory` (String) The absolute path of the account's directory on the web hosting.
- `id` (String) The username of the account, the same as `username`.
- `login` (String) The login to connect with, the username followed by `@` and the web hosting's domain.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_ftp_account.deploy
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/deploy"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<username>, or <hosting_id>/<username> when the provider sets
# organization_id and project_id. The password cannot be imported: the next apply sets the configured one.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_ftp_account.deploy 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/deploy
```
